# ceblar-20 v0.5

## Highlights

v0.5 extends the v0.4 ring-3 foundation with a live IRQ0 frame-aware scheduler, bounded ATA PIO storage, a raw `hda` VFS device, read-only FAT32 access, disk-backed ELF exec plumbing, blocking wait state transitions, page-walk user-pointer validation, and diagnostic shell process controls.

Two kernel workers are queued before init and are alternated by the PIT at 100 Hz. The worker run demonstrates independent process frames and 500 ms sleeps, while the original embedded user image still executes `SYS_WRITE` and emits `user: hello`.

## Storage

The primary-master ATA driver probes with IDENTIFY, bounds all waits, and exposes 28-bit LBA sector reads and writes. VFS reserves fd 3 for `hda`; FAT32 parses a direct BPB or an MBR FAT32 partition, follows cluster chains, performs root 8.3 lookup, reads file data, and enumerates root entries. The filesystem layer is deliberately read-only, while raw fd 3 supports sector writes for later experiments.

## Verification

```sh
make clean
make -j2
grub-file --is-x86-multiboot2 build/kernel.elf
make size
make test
```

`make test` runs a no-disk regression and, when `mkfs.fat` and `mcopy` are available, generates a 64 MiB fixture and runs a second QEMU boot with the disk attached. The storage boot emits `ata: primary master ready`, `fat32: mounted`, and `fat32: HELLO.TXT read ok`; both runs emit `user: hello` and both worker completion markers.

## Boundaries

This is an educational kernel release, not a production storage or process environment. ATA is polling-based, FAT32 supports a constrained root-directory read path, disk-backed exec has a bounded image size, wait/reaping has not yet gained complete resource reclamation, fork remains eager-copy, and the legacy cooperative context-switch assembly is retained but not used by the IRQ0 frame scheduler. Copy-on-write, complete mmap semantics, descriptor inheritance, and broader hardening remain v0.6 work.
